biography.plain_text: The Government of the Russian Federation is the federal executive institution. It operates through ministries and other federal bodies responsible for implementing legislation, administering national policy and coordinating public services. The name denotes the government collectively as a body and does not identify the prime minister, a minister, an agency head or another individual officeholder.

long_biography.plain_text:
Russia’s federal government is organised around a chairman, deputy chairmen and ministers whose portfolios cover national administration. The official government structure groups responsibilities across specialised ministries and services, allowing policy and implementation to be divided among distinct executive bodies.

Collective cabinet work provides coordination across those portfolios, while each body retains defined functions. Changes in personnel or departmental organisation do not alter the continuing identity of the Government of the Russian Federation. The name therefore describes the cabinet-level institution within the federal system and cannot be treated as the personal identity of its chairman, a minister or an agency leader.
